title: DBinder INCREFS/DECREFS and stub lifetime audit
scope: Read-only audit of the immutable communication_ipc commit bbb92dbb2f52aca54ab268307c9476ac1802f3ff, limited to DBINDER_INCREFS_TRANSACTION/DBINDER_DECREFS_TRANSACTION dispatch, the DBinderBaseInvoker::ProcessTransaction receive gate, caller identity tuple, app-auth map/refcount bookkeeping, and server-side session close cleanup. No code changes, tests, or PoCs.

verdict.reason: The receive path validates a caller identity and stub index against the per-process app-auth map before dispatch. The session bootstrap records the initial app/stub relation and takes one strong reference; INCREFS updates the live socket association; DECREFS removes the exact relation atomically and drops a strong reference only when that removal succeeds. Server-side socket close removes all relations for that socket under the same map lock and drops one reference for each removed relation. An in-flight transaction racing close could plausibly re-add stale state after cleanup, but this source-only review did not establish an attacker-controlled schedule, durable impact, or a reproducible violation, so it is not promoted as a finding.
verdict.not_a_product_validation: The source is pinned to the requested upstream commit, but deployed product build pairing is not established by this task.

pin.acquisition: Raw source files fetched by immutable commit URL; SHA-256 and Git blob IDs recomputed from downloaded bytes.

state_model.stub_relation_key: identity_key + stubIndex, with socketId as the current session binding
state_model.receive_authorization: CheckAndSetCallerInfo takes PID/UID/deviceId/tokenId from the current DBinderSessionObject, combines them with the transaction cookie (stubIndex) and socketId, then QueryAppInfoToStubIndex requires a matching relation whose socket is either 0 or the current socket. Only on success does it set DBinder caller-info fields.
state_model.initial_registration: InvokerDataBusThread adds the peer identity/stubIndex with socketId 0 and the local stub pointer; it calls IncStrongRef(this) only when AttachOrUpdateAppAuthInfo reports a newly added CommAuthInfo. The socketId 0 entry allows the first accepted data-bus session to pass the query gate.
state_model.increfs: DBinderIncRefsTransaction rejects local Binder calls, derives the tuple from the invoker's already validated caller info, and AttachOrUpdateAppAuthInfo updates the map relation to the active listenFd. This call supplies stub=nullptr, so this update does not acquire another stub strong reference.
state_model.decrefs: DBinderDecRefsTransaction builds the same tuple and calls DetachAppAuthInfo. Under appAuthMutex_, that operation erases only when both stubIndex and socketId match; it returns false otherwise. IPCObjectStub calls DecStrongRef(this) only after a successful erase.
state_model.session_close: OnDatabusSessionServerSideClosed calls DetachAppAuthInfoBySocketId, which holds appAuthMutex_ while removing CommAuthInfo and each map entry bound to the closing socket, returning one stubIndex per removed relation. The callback then takes objectMutex_, queries each surviving stub, and DecStrongRef(this) once per returned relation.

evidence.claim: The two special transaction codes dispatch to their dedicated handlers.
evidence.detail: DBINDER_INCREFS_TRANSACTION and DBINDER_DECREFS_TRANSACTION each dispatch to the corresponding DBinder handler when CONFIG_IPC_SINGLE is not defined.

evidence.claim: Transactions pass the caller-map gate before the target stub handler is invoked.
evidence.detail: ProcessTransaction calls CheckAndSetCallerInfo(listenFd, tr->cookie) before dispatch. TargetStubSendRequest then resolves tr->cookie to a registered stub under objectMutex_ and invokes SendRequest. Caller state is restored after request processing and on the allocator failure exits after it was set.

evidence.claim: Caller tuple and stub relation are checked against server-maintained session data.
evidence.location: CheckAndSetCallerInfo, around lines 753-782; QueryAppInfoToStubIndex(AppAuthInfo), around lines 1531-1548
evidence.detail: PID, UID, device ID and token ID come from the active DBinderSessionObject, not from the transaction parcel. The cookie supplies stubIndex. Query requires a tuple/stubIndex match and socketId either zero or equal to the active socket.

evidence.claim: The bootstrap route registers the peer relation and pins the stub before later transactions use it.
evidence.location: InvokerDataBusThread, around lines 600-650; AttachOrUpdateAppAuthInfo, around lines 1379-1420
evidence.detail: The validated INVOKE_LISTEN_THREAD setup obtains a stub index, inserts an appAuth relation using socketId 0, and IncStrongRef(this) only when a new CommAuthInfo is inserted. The socket-zero relation is explicitly accepted by QueryAppInfoToStubIndex and later updated to the active socket by INCREFS.

evidence.claim: DECREFS is idempotent with respect to a concurrent close removal for the same tuple/stub/socket relation.
evidence.location: DBinderDecRefsTransaction, around lines 246-277; DetachAppAuthInfo, around lines 1421-1455
evidence.detail: The strong reference is released only when DetachAppAuthInfo atomically finds the app tuple, stubIndex and matching socketId and erases that map entry. A racing removal that already took the entry makes the later detach return false.

evidence.claim: Server-side session cleanup owns the socket-bound relation removal and associated strong-ref release.
evidence.location: OnDatabusSessionServerSideClosed, around lines 607-628; DetachAppAuthInfoBySocketId, around lines 1477-1509
evidence.detail: Cleanup removes socket-bound entries under appAuthMutex_ and returns their stub indices. The invoker holds objectMutex_ while resolving surviving stub pointers and dropping one strong reference per removed relation.

review_limits: A transaction that passes CheckAndSetCallerInfo before a socket-close callback and mutates appAuth state after that callback could create an ordering-sensitive stale relation; this scout did not prove the schedule, impact, or attacker control. T30 should seek a deterministic lifecycle proof before treating it as a finding.

The per-invoker caller-info fields are mutable. This review did not establish whether one DBinderDatabusInvoker instance can process concurrent transactions, so no identity-race finding is claimed. T30 should verify invoker thread ownership if it considers this point.
Source-level checks do not prove product build inclusion or runtime SoftBus callback ordering.
t30_counterreview_questions: Can the incoming INVOKE_LISTEN_THREAD bootstrap be reached only through its local Binder and UID < ALLOWED_UID guard, and does its tuple/stubIndex relation precede remote transaction arrival?

Can a same-socket stale transaction pass CheckAndSetCallerInfo, then reinsert an appAuth entry after OnDatabusSessionServerSideClosed has removed that socket's entries? Establish ordering and user-visible/resource impact; otherwise classify as an unproven race.

Can two concurrent ProcessTransaction calls share a DBinderDatabusInvoker instance and interleave GetCallerInfo/CheckAndSetCallerInfo/SetCallerInfo/restore? Inspect ownership and thread dispatch; do not infer from mutable fields alone.

For one peer identity/stubIndex, verify duplicate INCREFS is idempotent and does not create additional strong refs, while distinct identity entries produce corresponding bootstrap strong refs and close decrements.
Confirm close cleanup and DECREFS cannot both decrement for one exact map entry; DetachAppAuthInfo and DetachAppAuthInfoBySocketId are expected to serialize through appAuthMutex_.
next_step: T30 independent counter-review of the bootstrap path, caller-state ownership, duplicate relation/refcount accounting, and close/DECREFS interleavings; keep candidate count at zero unless it establishes a deterministic, reachable violation.
